title: pinning-impact-scenarios-grid
content:
Purpose:

This note collects scenario-driven analysis of how model registry version pinning interacts with routing policies in a multi-region Redwood control plane. The goal is to surface operational edge-cases, define compatibility checks, and propose conservative fallback heuristics that the control plane can apply automatically.

Context and assumptions:
- We have three pinning scopes: session, route, and org/global. Route-level pins are the most common (feature flag / API route maps to a model+version).
- Registry stores model artifacts and metadata including: model family, architecture, tokenizers, input-shape limits, quantization profile (int8/4/pt), and region availability matrix (which regions have warmed VMs or cached artifacts).
- Routing policies include region affinity, cost-tier routing, and latency-SLO routing.
- Control plane can perform automated fallbacks (variant selection, region failover) when an exact pinned version is unavailable.

Core problems we observe:
1) Availability mismatch: a route pins v1.3 but only v1.2 is present in eu-west-1; us-west-2 has v1.3 but higher latency/cost.
2) API surface drift: v2.0 introduces a function-calling change (new structured output) that breaks downstream parsers. Pinning hides this for pinned customers but routing to fallback variants can break them.
3) Performance regression: quantized variant of pinned version has different latency characteristics causing SLO violations when autoscaler picks quantized nodes in a region.
4) KV cache incompatibility: models that differ in tokenizer or kv-cache layout cannot share warm caches, causing cache misses and tail latency.

Compatibility-check matrix (operational):
We use a simple graded matrix to determine whether a candidate model variant is a safe fallback for a pinned version:

Columns: candidate_variant | family_match | api_compat | tokenizer_compat | kv_cache_compat | quant_profile_diff | region_available | safe_score
Rows (examples):
1) v1.3-pt | yes | yes | yes | yes | none | eu-west-1=true | 100
2) v1.3-int8 | yes | yes | yes | no | int8_vs_pt | eu-west-1=true | 60
3) v1.2-pt | yes | maybe | yes | maybe | none | eu-west-1=true | 45
4) v1.3-pt | yes | yes | yes | yes | none | us-west-2=true | 80

Scoring guidance:
- family_match (required): if no, immediate reject for any auto-fallback.
- api_compat: yes=+30, maybe=+10, no=-inf (reject unless explicit override).
- tokenizer_compat: yes=+20, no=-inf (reject).
- kv_cache_compat: yes=+20, no=0 (acceptable but expect cache cold starts).
- quant_profile_diff: none=+10, small (pt->int8)=-10, large (fp16->int8)= -20 (may affect quality).
- region_available: yes=+10, if region incurs geo-cost/latency penalty then subtract accordingly.
- safe_score threshold: >=75 -> automatic fallback approved; 50-74 -> gated (require canary or manual approval); <50 -> reject.

Scenario analyses and recommended control plane behaviors:

Scenario A: regional outage where pinned version only exists in another region
- Symptoms: increasing 5xx for route, control plane detects artifact not cached in region.
- Recommendation: if safe_score >= 80 for candidate in other region, do region failover with traffic-weighted routing and priority for routes with latency SLO headroom. Emit customer-visible event and annotate request headers with "x-rw-fallback-region".
- If safe_score 50-79, spin up canary in target region (1% traffic) and evaluate end-to-end checks (schema validation, latency, correctness on small eval prompts) before widening.
- If <50, keep route in degraded state and surface manual migration playbook to the owner.

Scenario B: pinned version incompatible with new API surface of latest model
- Symptoms: downstream errors (parsing failures), increased error-rate for specific endpoints.
- Recommendation: treat api_compat=no as hard block for automated fallback. Provide a config toggle for "force-allow-incompatible-fallback" that requires org-admin approval and explicit opt-in per route. Also record a safety event and open a ticket to solutions-eng for client migration guidance.

Scenario C: quantization/regression surprise when autoscaler mixes node types
- Symptoms: SLO regressions but model correctness unchanged.
- Recommendation: Add a per-route runtime constraint: prefer "execution_profile" matches of pinned model (e.g., prefer pt nodes if pinned was pt). If mismatch is unavoidable, degrade to canary routing and enable extra token-level cost/latency telemetry to quickly detect regressions. Also auto-tag trace samples for retraining calibration.

Scenario D: cache/memory layout mismatch for long-chat sessions
- Symptoms: sudden spike in latency tails and mem pressure in nodes after routing change.
- Recommendation: Detect kv_cache_compat=false and either avoid multi-region fallback or, if fallback needed, warm the cache by replaying recent session prefixes (with privacy-safe sampling) before shifting significant traffic. Prefer session-scoped pinning where session tokens keep the exact variant.

Operational playbook (short):
- Before auto-fallback: run scoring function on candidate variants, fetch last-known eval artifacts, and ensure tokenizer hash matches.
- Canary plan: start at 0.5-1% traffic for 10–30 minutes; require no more than 10% delta in latency p95 and no schema errors.
- Escalation: if canary fails, rollback at control plane and create JIRA pinned to owner; notify SRE on-call if >5% error-rate.

Suggested telemetry and SLO hooks to add to Console:
- Per-route pinned-version availability metric (region by region).
- Safe_score per-potential-fallback (time-series).
- Canary health checks (schema validation rate, p95 latency, error-rate).
- Backfill cache-warm percent (est. fraction of sessions with warmed KV).

Migration patterns we encourage product teams to adopt:
- Prefer route-level pins for critical workflows; session pins for experiments that require exact reproducibility.
- Add a compatibility preflight job as part of model onboarding that computes tokenizer_hash, api_signature_hash, kv_layout_hash, and a region distribution estimate. Store these as immutable metadata in registry to speed control-plane decisions.
- For large rollouts, use staged pinning: pin test routes -> canary overlay -> global unpin (or pin-to-latest-if-passed).

Open questions and follow-ups:
- How to compute a meaningful "quality delta" metric automatically between quantized vs float variants? (Metric candidates: BLEU/ROUGE proxy on eval prompts, log-prob degradation on reference set.)
- Should we allow automated legal/regulatory region-sensitivity constraints to block region failover? (e.g., EU data residency).
- How to represent multi-model ensembles pinned at route-level when subset of models are unavailable? (Partial fallback semantics).

Action items:
- (Diego) prototype safe_score computation in registry service (JIRA-ENG-9803).
- (Lina) add tokenizer/hash preflight to onboarding pipeline (JIRA-ENG-9811).
- (Priya) draft control-plane canary rollout API and header conventions (PR target: registry-proto #319).

Notes: this doc is intentionally scenario-driven to help platform engineers reason about automated fallbacks and to guide product teams on safe pinning practices. Feedback welcome, particularly around threshold tuning and what additional signals should be mandatory for a safe auto-fallback.
